title: F. Next and Prev
statement:
Let p_1, …, p_n be a permutation of [1, …, n].

Let the q-subsequence of p be a permutation of [1, q], whose elements are in the same relative order as in p_1, …, p_n. That is, we extract all elements not exceeding q together from p in the original order, and they make the q-subsequence of p.

For a given array a, let pre(i) be the largest value satisfying pre(i) < i and a_{pre(i)} > a_i. If it does not exist, let pre(i) = -10^100. Let nxt(i) be the smallest value satisfying nxt(i) > i and a_{nxt(i)} > a_i. If it does not exist, let nxt(i) = 10^100.

For each q such that 1 ≤ q ≤ n, let a_1, …, a_q be the q-subsequence of p. For each i such that 1 ≤ i ≤ q, pre(i) and nxt(i) will be calculated as defined. Then, you will be given some integer values of x, and for each of them you have to calculate ∑limits_{i=1}^q min(nxt(i) - pre(i), x).

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1≤ t≤ 10^4). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains a single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 3·10^5) — the length of the permutation.

The second line of each test case contains n integers p_1, …, p_n (1 ≤ p_i ≤ n) — the initial permutation.

Then, for each q such that 1 ≤ q ≤ n in ascending order, you will be given an integer k (0 ≤ k ≤ 10^5), representing the number of queries for the q-subsequence. Then k numbers in a line follow: each of them is the value of x for a single query (1 ≤ x ≤ q).

It is guaranteed that the sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 3·10^5 and the sum of k over all test cases does not exceed 10^5.

For each test case, for each query, print a single line with an integer: the answer to the query.

The 1-subsequence is [1], and pre=[-10^100], nxt=[10^100]. ans(1)=min(10^100-(-10^100),1)=1.

The 5-subsequence is [1,4,3,2,5], and pre=[-10^100,-10^100,2,3,-10^100], nxt=[2,5,5,5,10^100]. ans(1)=5,ans(2)=10,ans(3)=14.

Input:
```
176 1 4 3 2 5 71 101 31 23 1 2 31 32 2 6
```

Output:
```
1
9
8
5
10
14
16
14
30
```
